source: AAA gasprices.aaa.com national average — $4.025 on Wednesday June 17, 2026 (Day 110), down from $4.065 (June 15) as crude fell to three-month lows on the US-Iran peace MOU that authorized a toll-free reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and removal of the US naval blockade. Still ~$1.04/gal above the $2.99 Feb 28 baseline (~35% higher). Brent settled $78.96 (first sub-$80 close since March) and WTI $76.05 on June 16 — a 3.5-month low. Pump relief from the June oil slide runs 2-3 weeks behind crude; NPR/AP (June 17) note higher gas, grocery and flight prices will likely outlast the war. Five states (Alaska, Hawaii, Nevada, Oregon, Washington) remain above $5; California is highest near $5.82; diesel ~$5.45. The May peak $4.536 (May 6, via Fox Business) stayed below AAA's all-time record of $5.016 (set June 14, 2022). Watson Institute / Costs of War (Brown): Americans have spent ~$318 more per household on gasoline and diesel since the war began (via CBS). Moody's Analytics (NPR, June 17) estimates the war has cost US consumers and taxpayers ~$132 billion so far.
